- File: scripts/ai_memory_lib.py
  Line or code reference: `_inject_token_into_url` (lines ~3040-3051) and `_resolve_origin_url` (lines ~3076-3087), interacting with the cleared `_git_subprocess_env` (lines ~2987-2992)
  Problem: the PR re-implements `_inject_token_into_url` to embed `GH_TOKEN` into the HTTPS clone URL (`https://x-access-token:TOKEN@github.com/...`) after `_git_subprocess_env` dropped the per-command `http.extraHeader` authentication, reversing the previously established credential-free-remote contract. The token now sits in the clone URL passed verbatim to the `git clone` subprocess in `_clone_for_memory_branch` and is written into the temp clone's `.git/config` by git itself.
  Runtime impact: the GitHub PAT leaks into subprocess arguments (visible via the process table while the clone runs), into any git error/diagnostic output that echoes the URL, and persists in the temporary clone's remote config — the exact leak the pre-PR header-based auth was built to avoid.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: scripts/memory_helpers.sh
  Line or code reference: `_memory_force_tick_remote_url` (lines ~575-588) and the clone/ls-remote/push call sites (lines ~612, ~769, ~885, ~919); also `memory_ensure_branch` (lines ~137-185)
  Problem: the force-tick remote builder now prints `https://x-access-token:TOKEN@host/repo` from `GH_PAT`/`GH_TOKEN` straight into clone/fetch arguments and, once `git remote add origin` runs inside the temp clone (line ~624), persists the token into that temp clone's git config. In `memory_ensure_branch` the `_memory_git` helper was also deleted, and `local token="${GH_TOKEN:-}"` is declared but never used — the branch-probe/creation path reverted to raw `git ls-remote` / `git push` against the original origin.
  Runtime impact: the token appears in process arguments, git diagnostics, and the temp clone config (a tempdir created by mktemp that is not guaranteed to be wiped on the fail-open `rm -rf` skip in callers), and in Actions the unauthenticated raw-push path cannot actually create the ai-memory branch when the origin carries no credentials.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: scripts/codex_helpers.sh
  Line or code reference: lines 365-374 (`model_provider_broker_prepare_codex_writer`'s else-branch) and lines 387-395 (`model_provider_broker_prepare_codex_readonly`), plus the forwarding in `codex_config_assemble` (lines 98-101, 143-145)
  Problem: both broker prepare functions invoke `scripts/write_codex_config.sh` with `--provider-base-url "${MODEL_PROVIDER_BROKER_BASE_URL}"`, but this PR removed that option from `scripts/write_codex_config.sh` (its `Usage:` block, the parser case list, and the generated `base_url` are now hardcoded to `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1`), so the writer's wildcard case errors `::error::write_codex_config.sh: unknown argument: --provider-base-url` and `exit 2`.
  Runtime impact: every broker-backed phase that regenerates an agent Codex config through these helpers — clarify, plan, implement, review editing, consolidator, summariser, validate, security-audit, workflow-log analysis, conflict resolution — dies before Codex ever launches, whenever the prepare path is exercised (i.e. on every fresh broker config generation).
